summary: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, install unidirectional sync trigger (note→customer_note), deploy new version state_only, then drop note column and trigger.
write_consistency: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger sets customer_note = COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, NEW.note), so old-version writes to note populate customer_note, while new-version writes to customer_note take precedence.
revision_notes: Removed the invalid SET DEFAULT note clause that caused PostgreSQL errors; replaced with trigger-only propagation. Previous bidirectional trigger caused cross-column leakage; this plan uses unidirectional note→customer_note sync.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, install unidirectional sync trigger.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, NEW.note); RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_to_customer_note_trg BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new Saleor version with a state-only migration; schema changes from expand are already in place.
Remove the sync trigger and the obsolete note column, leaving only customer_note.
sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS sync_note_to_customer_note_trg ON account_user;
ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; traffic now handled exclusively by the new version with customer_note.
